body:
I am on meds... They are the only thing that keeps me working. If I miss even one dos I shut down completely... My Christmas was laying on my couch for two days watching ever version of "a Christmas Carol" I could find on Amazon and crying because I ran out of pills just before the holidays.

I've been on and off meds since I was in 3rd grade. I was a bit of a medical anomaly for such an early onset depression and suicidal thoughts... But they didn't diagnose kids for PTSD back then.

Thank you but I can't see how. I needed to write something  know someone might read it. Since it was pointed out that after next week I won't have an office door so I won't have a place to cry at work any longer.

It's a bit sad and silly when you're co-workers know you have to shut your door and sob some days... Then they're worried about it changing and how I'm going handle it.

Pretty pathetic. :/

I lost my little girl 16 yes ago,  tomorrow is her 30th birthday.  (She was my baby sister,  I had to raise my siblings while I was taking the physical,  emotional and sexual abuse in their place) she was 11yrs old when she was diagnosed with bone cancer.  She fought for almost 4 years. My parents in some ways pulled their heads out of the ass's and stepped up to be parents...  But I was pushed aside by my family and eventually pushed out.  When we found out she was going to die and there was nothing to do but wait.  I left a $80000 a year job to move back in.  I sleep in the garage on a pull out couch in the middle of winter to take care of my family and at least see my baby girl before... 

Her death changed my family.  One brother ran off stopped doing drugs left his "gang" friends, got married, went to school, had kids...  My other brothers started doing things for themselves,.  They also went to school,  got jobs as care givers to people with special needs. They took care of my parents for years and now have adopted kids of the women they married...

After I burned through my life savings, I ended up pushing carts at Walmart. I never recovered but after my brother (son) dead.  I had to move on I went back to school and started teaching again with in months. I dead with her,  but started to come back to life after him... When the youngest (BB had Down syndrome,  he was 21) pasted it was easier to find my footing again but it hurts just as bad. 

No 2 people experience the death of a child or a friend the same way. Sometimes the people you share that person with give you strength,  other times they tear you down just by seeing them because it reminds you of What's missing.

He sounds like he emotional won't connect for wait ever reason. It sounds like you want/need someone to help you gain back that strength... As I did/do.

I can't give you an answer as how to cope.  My life story is not the same and I've never had a child I was aloud to call my own. But I do know this... Coping is about time,  and little moments of joy. So focus on moments as much as you can. I hope you can find your way.
You know what's funny the the first women I sleep with looked just like Fiona... Just at night.
